title: KCET 2012 Chemistry
subject: chemistry
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A1

questions.q: The mass of a non-volatile solute of molar mass 40 g mol$^{-1}$ that should be dissolved in 114 g of octane to lower its vapour pressure by 20% is
questions.explanation: By Raoult's law, $\dfrac{\Delta P}{P} = x_{solute}=0.2$. Moles of octane (M=114) = 1, so $n/(n+1)=0.2 \Rightarrow n=0.25$ mol, mass $=0.25\times40=10$ g.

questions.q: During the adsorption of a gas on the surface of a solid, which of the following is TRUE?
questions.explanation: Adsorption is spontaneous ($\Delta G<0$), exothermic ($\Delta H<0$), and randomness decreases as gas molecules settle on the surface ($\Delta S<0$).

questions.q: The approximate time duration in hours to electroplate 30 g of calcium from molten calcium chloride using a current of 5 amp is [At. mass of Ca = 40]
questions.explanation: Moles of Ca $=30/40=0.75$; charge needed $=0.75\times2\times96500=144750$ C; time $=144750/5=28950$ s $\approx 8$ hours.

questions.q: The pH of the solution obtained by mixing 100 ml of a solution of pH = 3 with 400 ml of a solution of pH = 4 is
questions.explanation: Total moles H$^+$ $=100\times10^{-3}\times10^{-3}+400\times10^{-3}\times10^{-4}=1.4\times10^{-4}$ mol in 0.5 L, so $[H^+]=2.8\times10^{-4}$ M, giving pH $=4-\log2.8$.

questions.q: The equilibrium constant of the reaction: A$_{(s)}$ + 2B$^+_{(aq)} \rightleftharpoons$ A$^{2+}_{(aq)}$ + 2B$_{(s)}$; E°$_{cell}$ = 0.0295 V is [$\dfrac{2.303RT}{F}=0.059$]
questions.explanation: n=2 electrons transferred; $E^\circ=\dfrac{0.059}{n}\log K \Rightarrow 0.0295=\dfrac{0.059}{2}\log K \Rightarrow \log K=1 \Rightarrow K=10$.

questions.q: An oxygen containing organic compound was found to contain 52% carbon and 13% of hydrogen. Its vapour density is 23. The compound reacts with sodium metal to liberate hydrogen. A functional isomer of this compound is
questions.explanation: Molecular mass $=2\times23=46$; %C and %H give C$_2$H$_6$O, i.e. ethanol (reacts with Na to release H$_2$). Its functional isomer is methoxymethane (dimethyl ether).

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT true regarding electromeric effect?
options: It results in the appearance of partial charges on the carbon atoms.
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: The electromeric effect causes complete transfer of a shared pair of pi-electrons to one atom, producing full (not partial) charges, so statement (1) is false.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT formed when a mixture of methyl bromide and bromobenzene is heated with sodium metal in the presence of dry Ether?
questions.explanation: Wurtz-Fittig reaction of CH$_3$Br and C$_6$H$_5$Br with Na gives ethane (CH$_3$-CH$_3$), toluene (CH$_3$-C$_6$H$_5$) and diphenyl (C$_6$H$_5$-C$_6$H$_5$); propane cannot form from these two reactants.

questions.q: Power alcohol is a mixture of
options: 80% Petrol + 20% Benzene + Small quantity of Ethanol
80% Petrol + 20% Ethanol + Small quantity of Benzene
80% Ethanol + 20% Benzene + Small quantity of Petrol
50% Petrol + 50% Ethanol + Small quantity of Benzene
questions.explanation: Power alcohol used as a motor fuel is a blend of about 80% petrol, 20% ethanol with a small quantity of benzene added as a co-solvent.

questions.q: Identify 'C' in the following: benzene + CH$_3$-CHCl-CH$_3$ $\xrightarrow[-HCl]{Anhyd\\ AlCl_3}$ A $\xrightarrow[130^\circ C]{O_2}$ B $\xrightarrow[100^\circ C]{dil\\ H_2SO_4}$ Phenol + C
questions.explanation: This is the cumene process: benzene + isopropyl chloride gives cumene (A), which is oxidised to cumene hydroperoxide (B), and acid hydrolysis gives phenol + acetone (C).

questions.q: 20 ml of methane is completely burnt using 50 ml of oxygen. The volume of the gas left after cooling to room temperature is
questions.explanation: CH$_4$+2O$_2\rightarrow$CO$_2$+2H$_2$O; 20 ml CH$_4$ needs 40 ml O$_2$, leaving 10 ml O$_2$ unused, plus 20 ml CO$_2$ formed (water condenses on cooling) = 30 ml total gas left.

questions.q: 100 ml of 0.1 M acetic acid is completely neutralized using a standard solution of NaOH. The volume of Ethane obtained at STP after the complete electrolysis of the resulting solution is
questions.explanation: Moles of CH$_3$COONa formed = 0.01. Kolbe electrolysis: 2CH$_3$COO$^-\rightarrow$C$_2$H$_6$+2CO$_2$+2e$^-$, giving 0.005 mol ethane = $0.005\times22400=112$ ml at STP.

questions.q: Saccharin, an artificial sweetner, is manufactured from
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: Chemistry in Everyday Life
questions.explanation: Saccharin is industrially manufactured starting from toluene through sulfonation and further reactions.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT TRUE for S$_N$1 reaction?
options: 3° − alkyl halides generally react through S$_N$1 reaction.
The rate of the reaction does not depend upon the molar concentration of the nucleophile.
1° − alkyl halides generally react through S$_N$1 reaction.
questions.explanation: S$_N$1 reactions proceed via a stable carbocation, favoured by 3° alkyl halides; 1° alkyl halides do not readily undergo S$_N$1, so statement (4) is false.

questions.q: Oil of winter green is
questions.explanation: Oil of wintergreen is methyl salicylate, an ester of salicylic acid.

questions.q: An organic compound 'A' burns with a sooty flame. It is negative towards Tollen's reagent test and positive for Borsche's reagent test. The compound 'A' is
questions.explanation: A sooty flame indicates an aromatic compound; a negative Tollen's test rules out an aldehyde, and a positive Borsche's reagent test (for aromatic methyl ketones) identifies it as acetophenone.

questions.q: For a reaction: A + B → Products, the rate of the reaction at various concentrations are given below: [table: Expt1 A=0.2,B=0.2,rate=2; Expt2 A=0.2,B=0.4,rate=4; Expt3 A=0.6,B=0.4,rate=36] The rate law for the above reaction is
questions.explanation: Comparing expts 1 & 2 (A constant, B doubles, rate doubles): order in B = 1. Comparing expts 2 & 3 (B constant, A triples, rate increases 9×): order in A = 2. Rate law: r=K[A]$^2$[B].

questions.q: Which one of the following has NO unpaired electrons?
questions.explanation: By molecular orbital theory, the peroxide ion O$_2^{2-}$ has both antibonding $\pi^*$ orbitals completely filled, giving no unpaired electrons.

questions.q: The atomic number of cobalt is 27. The EAN of cobalt in Na$_3$[Co(NO$_2$)$_4$Cl$_2$] is
questions.explanation: Co is in +3 state (losing 3 electrons: Z-3=24), and EAN = 24 + 2×(coordination number 6) = 24+12=36.

questions.q: The 'spin only' magnetic moment of Ni$^{2+}$ in aqueous solution would be [At. No. of Ni = 28]
questions.explanation: Ni$^{2+}$ (d$^8$) has 2 unpaired electrons; $\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=\sqrt{2\times4}=\sqrt8$ BM.

questions.q: Impossible orbital among the following is
questions.explanation: For n=3, l can be 0,1,2 (s,p,d) only; f (l=3) requires n≥4, so 3f cannot exist.

questions.q: The total number of electrons in 18 ml of water (density = 1 g ml$^{-1}$) is
questions.explanation: 18 ml water = 18 g = 1 mole = 6.02×10$^{23}$ molecules; each H$_2$O has 10 electrons, so total = 10×6.02×10$^{23}$=6.02×10$^{24}$.

questions.q: The number of moles of hydrogen that can be added to 1 mole of an oil is the highest in
questions.explanation: Linseed oil has the highest degree of unsaturation (highest iodine value) among these oils, so it can add the most hydrogen on hydrogenation.

questions.q: The reaction between sodium and water can be made less vigorous by
questions.explanation: Amalgamating sodium with mercury reduces its reactivity by lowering the effective concentration of free sodium, making its reaction with water less vigorous.

questions.q: All colloidal dispersions have
questions.explanation: Colloidal particles are large and fewer in number per unit volume than in true solutions, giving colloidal dispersions a low osmotic pressure.

questions.q: Silver iodide is used for producing artificial rain because AgI
options: is easy to spray at high altitude
has crystal structure similar to ice
questions.explanation: AgI has a crystal structure similar to ice, so it acts as a nucleating agent for the condensation of water vapour into ice crystals, inducing rain (cloud seeding).

questions.q: The equilibrium constant of a reaction is 0.008 at 298 K. The standard free energy change of the reaction at the same temperature is
questions.explanation: $\Delta G^\circ=-RT\ln K=-8.314\times298\times\ln(0.008)\approx+11.96$ kJ (K<1 gives positive $\Delta G^\circ$).

questions.q: The function of potassium ethyl xanthate in froth floatation process is to make the ore
questions.explanation: Potassium ethyl xanthate is a collector that coats the ore particles, making them water repellent (hydrophobic) so they attach to air bubbles and float in the froth.

questions.q: The correct order of electronegativities of N, O, F & P is
questions.explanation: Electronegativity increases across a period and decreases down a group: F(4.0) > O(3.5) > N(3.0) > P(2.1).

questions.q: The s-block element used as a catalyst in the manufacture of Buna-S rubber is
questions.explanation: Sodium metal is used as a catalyst in the polymerisation of butadiene and styrene to manufacture Buna-S rubber.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a covalent compound?
options: Small difference in electronegativity between the combining atoms.
questions.explanation: Covalent compounds have definite molecular geometry due to directional bonding, so 'no definite geometry' is not a characteristic of covalent compounds.

questions.q: The volume of 0.1 M oxalic acid that can be completely oxidized by 20 ml of 0.025 M KMnO$_4$ solution is
questions.explanation: Using $n_1M_1V_1=n_2M_2V_2$ with n(oxalic acid)=2, n(KMnO$_4$)=5: $2\times0.1\times V=5\times0.025\times20 \Rightarrow V=12.5$ ml.

questions.q: A ligand is
options: either a Lewis acid or a Lewis base
questions.explanation: A ligand donates an electron pair to the central metal atom/ion, so it acts as a Lewis base.

questions.q: The vapour pressures of two liquids A and B in their pure states are in the ratio of 1 : 2. A binary solution of A and B contains A and B in the mole proportion of 1 : 2. The mole fraction of A in the vapour phase of the solution will be
questions.explanation: Take $P_A^\circ=p, P_B^\circ=2p$, $x_A=1/3, x_B=2/3$. Partial pressures: $P_A=p/3, P_B=4p/3$. Mole fraction of A in vapour $=\dfrac{p/3}{p/3+4p/3}=\dfrac{1}{5}=0.2$.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: The total entropy of the universe remains constant.
The total entropy of the universe is continuously decreasing.
The total energy of the universe is continuously decreasing.
The total energy of the universe remains constant.
questions.explanation: By the first law of thermodynamics (law of conservation of energy), the total energy of the universe remains constant.

questions.q: 5 ml of 0.4 N NaOH is mixed with 20 ml of 0.1 N HCl. The pH of the resulting solution will be
questions.explanation: Milliequivalents of NaOH $=5\times0.4=2$; of HCl $=20\times0.1=2$; they exactly neutralize each other giving a neutral solution, pH = 7.

questions.q: On adding which of the following, the pH of 20 ml of 0.1 N HCl will not alter?
questions.explanation: 0.1 N HCl has pH = 1; adding 500 ml of HCl of the same pH (=1, i.e. same [H$^+$]) does not change the pH of the solution.

questions.q: Which one of the following has a potential more than zero?
questions.explanation: For a hydrogen electrode, $E=-0.059\log[H^+]^{-1}$-type relation gives E=0 at 1M HCl (standard); at concentration greater than 1 M (2 M), the electrode potential becomes positive (greater than zero) relative to the standard hydrogen electrode.

questions.q: HCHO was treated with a reagent X. The product formed upon hydrolysis in the presence of an acid gave C$_2$H$_5$OH. The reagent X is
questions.explanation: CH$_3$MgI (Grignard reagent) reacts with HCHO to form CH$_3$CH$_2$OMgI, which on acid hydrolysis gives ethanol (C$_2$H$_5$OH).

questions.q: Benzylamine is a stronger base than aniline because
options: The lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom in benzylamine is delocalised.
The lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom in aniline is delocalised.
The lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom in aniline is not involved in resonance.
Benzylamine has a higher molecular mass than aniline.
questions.explanation: In aniline, the lone pair on N is delocalised into the benzene ring (resonance), reducing its availability for protonation, making aniline a weaker base than benzylamine, where the N lone pair is fully available.

questions.q: The relative acidic strengths of benzoic acid, o-toluic acid and p-toluic acid is of the decreasing order:
options: p-toluic acid > o-toluic acid > benzoic acid
o-toluic acid > p-toluic acid > benzoic acid
p-toluic acid > benzoic acid > o-toluic acid
o-toluic acid > benzoic acid > p-toluic acid
questions.explanation: The electron-donating methyl group decreases acidity relative to benzoic acid, and the ortho effect makes o-toluic acid more acidic than p-toluic acid, giving the order o-toluic acid > benzoic acid > p-toluic acid.

questions.q: The C-H bond and C-C bond in ethane are formed by which of the following types of overlap?
questions.explanation: Each carbon in ethane is sp$^3$ hybridised; C-H bonds form by sp$^3$-s overlap and the C-C bond forms by sp$^3$-sp$^3$ overlap.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of CH$_3$-CH(OH)-CH$_2$-CHO [pent-2-... structure with OH and C=O] is
questions.explanation: The compound is a pentanone chain with a ketone at C2 and hydroxyl at C4; the principal characteristic group (ketone) gets the lowest locant, giving 4-hydroxy-2-pentanone.

questions.q: A first order reaction is 60% complete in 20 minutes. How long will the reaction take to be 84% complete?
questions.explanation: $k=\dfrac{2.303}{20}\log\dfrac{100}{40}$. For 84% completion, $t=\dfrac{2.303}{k}\log\dfrac{100}{16}$. Since $100/16=(100/40)^2$ approx, $t\approx2\times20=40$ minutes.

questions.q: A given sample of milk turns sour at room temperature (27 °C) in 5 hours. In a refrigerator at −3 °C, it can be stored 10 times longer. The energy of activation for the souring of milk is
questions.explanation: $T_1=270K, T_2=300K$, $k_2/k_1=10$ (10× longer at lower temperature means 10× slower rate). $\ln(k_2/k_1)=\dfrac{E_a}{R}\dfrac{T_2-T_1}{T_1T_2}\Rightarrow2.303=\dfrac{E_a}{R}\times\dfrac{30}{270\times300}$, giving $E_a=2.303\times2700R$ J/mol $=2.303\times2.7R$ kJ/mol.

questions.q: At 300 K, a gaseous reaction: A → B + C was found to follow first order kinetics. Starting with pure A, the total pressure at the end of 20 minutes was 100 mm of Hg. The total pressure after the completion of the reaction is 180 mm of Hg. The partial pressure of A (in mm of Hg) is
questions.explanation: Initial pressure of A, $P_0=90$ mm (since total pressure doubles to 180 as A fully decomposes to B+C). At t=20 min, $P_t=P_0+x=100$, so $x=10$; partial pressure of A remaining $=P_0-x=90-10=80$ mm.

questions.q: From the Ellingham graphs on carbon, which of the following statements is FALSE?
options: CO$_2$ is more stable than CO at less than 983 K
CO reduces Fe$_2$O$_3$ to Fe at less than 983 K
CO is less stable than CO$_2$ at more than 983 K
CO reduces Fe$_2$O$_3$ to Fe in the reduction zone of Blast furnace
questions.explanation: On the Ellingham diagram for carbon, above 983 K the C/CO line drops below the CO/CO$_2$ line, meaning CO becomes more stable (not less stable) than CO$_2$ above 983 K, so statement (3) is false.

questions.q: Which of the following is a negatively charged bidentate ligand?
questions.explanation: Dimethylglyoximato ion is a bidentate ligand binding through two deprotonated oxygen atoms and carries a negative charge; cyano is monodentate, ethylenediamine is neutral bidentate, acetato is monodentate/negatively charged.

questions.q: The secondary valency of platinum in tetra ammine dichloroplatinum (IV) chloride is
questions.explanation: In [Pt(NH$_3$)$_4$Cl$_2$]Cl$_2$, platinum is coordinated to 4 NH$_3$ and 2 Cl ligands, giving a secondary valency (coordination number) of 6.

questions.q: Which one of the following has a magnetic moment of 1.75 BM?
questions.explanation: Ti$^{3+}$ (d$^1$) has one unpaired electron; $\mu=\sqrt{1\times3}=\sqrt3\approx1.73\approx1.75$ BM.

questions.q: The correct order of ionisation energy of C, N, O & F is
questions.explanation: Ionisation energies: C≈1086, O≈1314, N≈1402, F≈1681 kJ/mol. N has extra stability from a half-filled 2p$^3$ configuration, raising its IE above O's, giving the order C < O < N < F.

questions.q: The correct set of four quantum numbers for the outermost electron of sodium (Z = 11) is
questions.explanation: Sodium's outermost electron is in 3s$^1$: n=3, l=0 (s-orbital), m=0, s=+½.

questions.q: The ore that is concentrated by the Froth Floatation process is
questions.explanation: Froth floatation is used for sulphide ores; chalcopyrite (CuFeS$_2$) is a sulphide ore concentrated by this method.

questions.q: The equivalent mass of a certain bivalent metal is 20. The molecular mass of its anhydrous chloride is
questions.explanation: Atomic mass of metal = equivalent mass × valency = 20×2=40. Chloride MCl$_2$: molecular mass $=40+2\times35.5=111$.

questions.q: 2 moles of N$_2$O$_4$(g) is kept in a closed container at 298 K and under 1 atm pressure. It is heated to 596 K when 20% by mass of N$_2$O$_4$(g) decomposes to NO$_2$. The resulting pressure is
questions.explanation: N$_2$O$_4\rightleftharpoons2NO_2$; 20% of 2 mol = 0.4 mol dissociates, giving 1.6 mol N$_2$O$_4$ left + 0.8 mol NO$_2$ = 2.4 mol total (n$_1$=2 initially). Using $\dfrac{P_1V}{n_1T_1}=\dfrac{P_2V}{n_2T_2}$: $P_2=1\times\dfrac{2.4}{2}\times\dfrac{596}{298}=2.4$ atm.

questions.q: Sucrose is NOT a reducing sugar since
options: it contains no free aldehyde or keto group adjacent to a CHOH group
it is built up of a fructose unit
questions.explanation: In sucrose, both the anomeric carbons of glucose and fructose are involved in the glycosidic bond, leaving no free aldehyde or ketone group, so it cannot reduce Fehling's/Tollen's reagent.

questions.q: Which one of the following contains ionic, covalent and co-ordinate bonds?
questions.note: In CN- the carbon atom carries the terminal lone pair and formal negative charge (:C≡N:-), so Na+ bonds ionically to carbon, giving the standard compound NaCN (option C) with an ionic Na-C bond, a covalent C-N bond, and one coordinate bond within the triple bond (N donating a lone pair to C); KEA's key instead credits NaNC (option D).
questions.explanation: Na-N/C bond is ionic, the C≡N triple bond is covalent, and one of the bonds in the triple bond arises from a coordinate (dative) lone pair donation; KEA's key credits this combination to NaNC (as per KEA key).

questions.q: Dialysis can be used to separate
questions.explanation: Dialysis separates colloidal particles (like proteins) from crystalloids/small molecules (like glucose) using a semipermeable membrane, since glucose passes through while protein does not.

questions.q: The percentage of p-character of the hybrid orbitals in graphite and diamond are respectively:
questions.explanation: Graphite carbon is sp$^2$ hybridised (p-character = 2/3 = 67%); diamond carbon is sp$^3$ hybridised (p-character = 3/4 = 75%).

questions.q: A gas expands from a volume of 1 m$^3$ to a volume of 2 m$^3$ against an external pressure of 10$^5$ Nm$^{-2}$. The work done by the gas will be
